SEOUL, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have rejected a proposal by Korea Electric Power Corp to make a 25 trillion won ($18.7 billion) upfront payment to support power supplies for planned semiconductor mega clusters, according to a document submitted to a lawmaker. Here are some details: 

• The two chipmakers told the state-run utility company it would be difficult to accept the proposal following internal reviews, according to the document, which was shared with Reuters by the office of lawmaker Lee Chul-gyu.

• The companies were unsure if such large upfront payments were necessary, citing uncertainty over the long-term durability of semiconductor demand, a company official in Seoul told Reuters. The official spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

• Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix declined to comment.

• South Korean newspaper Chosun Ilbo reported earlier this month that KEPCO had proposed that the chipmakers make the advance payment for electricity expected to be consumed by new chip fabrication plants, in order to allow the utility company to invest in infrastructure to power the plants.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SEOUL, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have rejected a proposal by Korea Electric Power Corp to make a 25 trillion won ($18.7 billion) upfront payment to support power supplies for planned semiconductor mega clusters, according to a document submitted to a lawmaker. Here are some details: 

o The two chipmakers told the state-run utility company it would be difficult to accept the proposal following internal reviews, according to the document, which was shared with Reuters by the office of lawmaker Lee Chul-gyu.

o The companies were unsure if such large upfront payments were necessary, citing uncertainty over the long-term durability of semiconductor demand, a company official in Seoul told Reuters. The official spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

o Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix declined to comment.

o South Korean newspaper Chosun Ilbo reported earlier this month that KEPCO had proposed that the chipmakers make the advance payment for electricity expected to be consumed by new chip fabrication plants, in order to allow the utility company to invest in infrastructure to power the plants.

(Reporting by Heejin KimEditing by Ed Davies)

SEOUL, Sept 18 (Reuters) - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Friday that concerns over the commercial viability of a planned US investment package under its trade deal with Washington had become a sticking point in negotiations, although the two sides were nearing an agreement.

Lee told a news conference some elements of the package were difficult for Seoul to accept, but said the government would continue discussions to ensure any deal protects South Korea's interests while benefiting both countries and the broader US-South Korea relationship.

The allies have continued negotiations on implementing a trade deal struck last year, under which Seoul committed to invest $350 billion in US manufacturing in return for lowering tariffs on Korean imports to 15%.

# Samsung y SK Hynix rechazan la propuesta de KEPCO de adelantar 18.700 millones USD para el suministro eléctrico

Publicado el 14/09/2026 a 04:51 - Modificado el 14/09/2026 a 04:52

Reuters - Traducido por Marketscreener

Samsung Electronics y SK Hynix han rechazado una propuesta de Korea Electric Power Corp para realizar un pago anticipado de 25 billones de wones (18.700 millones USD) destinado a financiar el suministro eléctrico de los futuros macrocomplejos de semiconductores, según revela un documento remitido a un legislador. Estos son los detalles principales:

o Los dos fabricantes de chips comunicaron a la eléctrica estatal que, tras realizar sendas revisiones internas, les resultaría difícil aceptar la propuesta, de acuerdo con el documento facilitado a Reuters por la oficina del parlamentario Lee Chul-gyu.

o Las compañías no tienen la certeza de que unos pagos anticipados de tal magnitud sean necesarios, dada la incertidumbre sobre la sostenibilidad de la demanda de semiconductores a largo plazo, según explicó a Reuters un directivo de una de las empresas en Seúl. La fuente pidió mantener el anonimato debido a la sensibilidad del asunto.

o Samsung Electronics y SK Hynix declinaron hacer comentarios al respecto.

o El diario surcoreano Chosun Ilbo informó a principios de este mes de que KEPCO había propuesto a los fabricantes de chips este pago por adelantado sobre el consumo eléctrico previsto en las nuevas plantas de fabricación. El objetivo de la eléctrica era obtener fondos para invertir en la infraestructura necesaria para abastecer dichas instalaciones.
